scope: Primary-paper research; historical architecture and reported results, not a modern SDK benchmark.

papers.title: AFlow: Automating Agentic Workflow Generation
papers.mechanism: Offline search over complete executable workflows. MCTS tree nodes are whole workflows; an optimizer edits prompts and code connections. Model, temperature and output format stay fixed. Reusable operators narrow the search. Mixed uniform/score selection, repeated execution evaluation, and parent-linked experience guide subsequent edits.
papers.discovered_workflow: MBPP: generate three programs; ensemble-select; test; return on success, otherwise repair using failure feedback.

result.recommended_chart: MBPP only; avoid averaging incompatible benchmark metrics.
result.denominator_note: Exact MBPP test count undisclosed in paper. Full dataset split 20% validation/80% test, seed 42; do not substitute the standard MBPP test size.

papers.limits: Requires numerical evaluation; validation-driven workflow discovery has search cost. Results concern benchmark workflows. Different executors may need different workflows.

repository_workflow.source_notes: Current run.py automatically downloads datasets. Its validation_rounds default is 1, unlike the paper's 5: pass 5 explicitly. README warns some operators may have migration bugs. Current code defaults do not establish exact paper reproduction.

papers.teaching_inference: Treat this as outer-loop process improvement: first define a reliable score, then compare candidate procedures on held-out examples. AFlow's optimized workflow is the deployed artifact; the search tree is not the user's live task state.

papers.title: Language Agent Tree Search Unifies Reasoning, Acting, and Planning in Language Models
papers.mechanism: Online trajectory search. States contain task, action history and observations. UCT selects; the LM samples actions; environment feedback plus LM/self-consistency scoring evaluates children. Simulate, backpropagate reward, and retain failed trajectories with reflections as future context. Stop on success or budget. No weight training or learned world model.

result.recommended_chart: WebShop score among prompting methods; success rate is a separate metric.
result.locator: Table 6 and Section 5.3, p.8; Appendix D.3, pp.16–17
result.comparison_note: LATS, ReAct best-of-k and Reflexion share k=30, not equal model-call/token budgets. Other Table 6 training/human rows are not controlled same-model comparisons.

papers.limits: Higher inference cost than simpler prompting; requires reverting environments to earlier states. Benchmarks simplify real-world interaction.

papers.teaching_inference: For a utility operator, branch and replay in a simulator or reversible workspace. Search over draft actions; commit real-world changes only after selecting an outcome. The paper does not establish safe rollback of irreversible external actions.

synthesis: AFlow searches for the procedure used across tasks; LATS searches alternative paths within a task. An orchestration SDK can implement either control structure but does not automatically supply its evaluator, budget, reversible environment or evidence of improvement.
